name: James Hawkins
profile: British co-founder, with Tim Glaser, of PostHog, the open-source product-analytics and 'product OS' platform born in Y Combinator's W20 batch. PostHog has grown into session replay, feature flags, experiments, a data warehouse and AI tools, and claims 100,000+ customers. It has been cash-flow positive since Dec 2024, raised a Stripe-led $70M Series D (2025) and a $75M Series E (Oct 2025), and is valued at $1B+.
interesting_fact: PostHog says 54% of YC's first 2024 batch adopted it, making it one of the top three products used by YC companies. It is famous for an entirely public company handbook and a quirky hedgehog brand.
deep_cut_fact: PostHog's famous public handbook began as a hack. Before launching on Hacker News, Hawkins and Glaser wanted to 'look as mature as possible' with big footers like big, boring companies, so they wrote up how they wanted to work to fill the links.
notes: Very public, writes openly about running PostHog (handbook, newsletter, X), so a strong podcast candidate. The founders' first idea (Aug 2019) was a tool for managing technical debt, which failed before PostHog.
